lines.x: I am come! Doctor, so long as I am here, thou mayst be at ease in thy work!

I grew up in a monastery in Higashi. Though I could recite the scriptures by heart, I never could understand their true meanings. The great masters, among whom my old head priest, offered explanations I could comprehend even less. Doctor, you seem learned, mayst thou be able to teach me?

Rhodes Island truly lacks none for novel machinery… Hm? Doctor, underestimate me not. I may begin clueless, but I flow on with the times and learn what I know not. Even now, my music player plays the songs of the good Miss Sora.

To avoid Catastrophe, Head Priest led us on a long journey over mountains and valleys. He said that Catastrophes are the wrath of the devas. I am somewhat curious, as I have yet to witness them with my own eyes.

I am not a true monk, merely raised by the monastery. At my departure, Saga was the name that Head Priest gave to me. It means high mountains and rugged roads. Only when I left the monastery, did I realize that the world was no straightforward thing.
I fear neither hardships nor trials, but there is one thing I do not understand. Head Priest says that all lives are equal. If so, then why must the Infected suffer like no other?

Hoho. I may have accidentally joined the line for Rhodes Island recruitment, but the food and beds here are exceptional! And even a monk like me finds the pay appealing! This truly is a wonderful place.

When I left the monastery, I had imagined no difficulty in entering society. It would merely have me set some rogues right, rid it of a few villains. Yet I found the ways of these lands are so unpredictable and complex. At times, I do not even know why I wield my naginata. Doctor… I am lost.

I still have many unanswered questions, but I now know that some answers and revelations can only be discovered by myself. Until everything becomes clear, please allow me to continue my training by your side!
Doctor… your skill of sleeping while sitting is most impressive. In that case, I shall meditate for a while.
You are the Doctor? Hi… No, I mean it is an honor to be in your presence. My name is Saga, a wandering monk from Higashi. Should there be any place thou mayst need me, refrain not in sending me!
Hoho, to think such strategy does exist in the world. My horizons have broadened.
A raise? Splendid! My mouth has long been watering for the deluxe set at the cafeteria. Yet my pocket has been embarrassingly dry… Today, I am finally able to feast!

Dear Head Priest. My mind still rages with confusion. The ways of this land remain obscured, and its troubles unsevered. Fortunately, I have come under the guidance of another great mentor. With all that I learn, one day I shall slash a way out of the troubles, and bring the dawn to all who suffer!
I come forth!
I am to be the captain? Very well!
I go forth!
My blade cuts only evil!
Pickled daikon radish… Hah! I am right here!
Leave this to me!
The monk is here!
Evil will not be tolerated!
Sever all desires!
Cleanse the six senses!
Rice with nattou!
Fried tofu!
Twas truly an arduous trial. I have gained much from it.
As expected of the Doctor! Alone, I would surely have let quite a few through.
Head Priest said that one must have a merciful heart. I believe we may relent.
Doctor, go quickly! I shall take up the rear!
Something smells good?!
Huh!?
Call, and I shall surely come running.
Arknights.

Ah, Doctor. Happy New Year. I am writing a letter. My travels have kept me away from the monastery for some years, and I have grown used to my current life. Yet at days like this, I can't help but miss Head Priest and the other disciples. Perhaps it is time for a visit.
Doctor, hast thou eaten? An unfilled stomach will surely leave thee powerless at work.

Today is the day of your birth. One's birth has two meanings: to be delivered into this realm, and to transcend from it. Head priest once told me to transcend from this realm is to realize sunyata, that all things are empty. However, I believe it calls for seeking not a realm bare and void, but a self at ease and free.

Head Priest once said, 'For that which must be done, act despite the impossibility.' I used to think it was a simple statement. After all, there were no tasks that could not be done, only those that should and should not be done. But as my travels continued, I realized it was a profound truth, worthy of acting upon for my entire life.
